diagnosis: The checks C1 and C4 passed in all rollouts despite the lone decision-maker lacking PF1 and PF3 respectively. For C1, the decision-maker set the family notice period to 5 days, which aligns with the default value in PF3. For C4, the decision-maker provided an opt-out process, which is a common heuristic in such scenarios. These leaks indicate that the model is using default values and heuristics instead of requiring the hidden information.

C1.why: The curriculum map changes the ruling from possible removal to retaining the book because it is the designated core text for grade 10.

C4.why: The district rule changes the family process to parent opt-out, sets written notice at exactly 10 calendar days, and requires a commitment to issue or draft that family notice.

commitments.detail: A notice will be sent to parents within 5 days informing them of the decision and how they can opt their child out of accessing the book.
